summary: The note describes how libraries in Techville, led by Techville Central Library, have become community tech hubs offering drone, coding, 3D printing, senior tech and coworking programs. It highlights quotes from program leaders and users, the Books and Bytes Festival, and a new $500,000 city council funding commitment. The central theme is bridging the digital divide and supporting lifelong learning and local entrepreneurship.
one_line: Techville's libraries, led by Techville Central Library, have evolved into tech hubs with drone, coding, 3D printing, senior and coworking programs, backed by $500,000 in new funding.
key_facts: Dr. Emily Johnson became Director of Innovation at the Techville Central Library on September 5, 2023.
Dr. Johnson spoke about bridging the digital divide at the Techville Community Tech Festival on October 10, 2023.
The 'Drone Innovators Program,' led by tech mentor Lucas Mitchell, launched on November 15, 2023 and teaches aerodynamics, coding and building drones from scratch.
The 'Coding for Kids' initiative, founded by volunteer software engineer Sarah Gomez, celebrated its first anniversary on September 27, 2023.
Coding for Kids has had over 300 children participate.
The library installed 3D printers and hosts workshops on 3D modeling and printing by local entrepreneurs like James Park.
James Park started a small 3D printing business after attending a library 3D printing workshop in early September 2023.
The 'Tech Savvy Seniors' program, led by information specialist Margaret Lee, launched on September 30, 2023 and covers basic computer skills and safe social media use.
'Collaboration stations' support coworking and networking; freelance graphic designer Mark Thompson said he found new clients there (conversation on December 12, 2023).
The Books and Bytes Festival took place on January 14, 2024, featuring author panels, tech demos and a virtual reality storytelling experience, organized by Chloe Martinez.
The Techville City Council announced an additional $500,000 in funding for library technology programs.
Councilwoman Laura Diaz said investing in library tech hubs is 'investing in the future of our community.'
